# Appāyuka Sutta (Ud 5.2 (PTS Ud 47))

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Appāyuka Sutta* is the second discourse of the fifth chapter (*Soṇavagga*) of the *Udāna* (Ud 5.2, PTS Ud 47) [SuttaCentral]. In this sutta, Venerable Ānanda remarks with wonder on how short-lived the mother of the Blessed One was, noting that she passed away seven days after the Buddha was born (*acchariyam bhante, abbhutam, bhante, yāvad appāyukā hi bhante bhagavato mātā ahosi*) [SuttaCentral; Analayo, Genesis of the bodhisattva ideal; Nyanatusita 2013]. In response, the Buddha explains that mothers of all bodhisattas are short-lived (*appāyukā hi bodhisattamātaro honti*), dying seven days after their sons are born and arising in the Tusita heaven (*Tusitaṁ kāyaṁ*) [Endo 1997; Masefield 1997]. Toshiichi Endo observes that this is one of the rare instances where the term *bodhisatta* appears in the *Udāna*, where the mother's lifespan is presented as an inherent constant or cosmic principle (*dhammatā*) applicable to the mothers of all Buddhas [Endo 1997].
